concept: Per-node and per-shard $indexStats aggregation across replica sets and shards
summary: Source-anchored research for Per-node and per-shard $indexStats aggregation across replica sets and shards. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: A zero ops count means the index was not used since the counter started (index creation or server restart), with exceptions. Before dropping an index, analyze every replica set member and make sure the counter has collected for a considerable amount of time, because an index used only once a month for heavy reporting can be wrongly dropped. Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/advisors/checks/mongodb-unused-indexes.html ; https://www.percona.com/blog/identifying-unused-indexes-in-mongodb/
Results identify the mongod host and, for sharded deployments, the shard. Keep both identities when collecting per-index measurements. (high confidence)

Index counters reset on mongod restart, index drop/recreation, or modification with collMod. Preserve accesses.since when comparing samples; raw cumulative counts from different observation windows are not directly comparable. (high confidence)

Methodological inference: $indexStats accesses counters apply only to the node where the query runs, and each carries its own since timestamp (counters reset on mongod restart, index drop/recreation, or collMod on the index). Collect per-host samples before grouping by shard and index, and compare intervals only when the since values match; a shard rollup otherwise can hide unsampled members. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexStats.md

Run db.collection.aggregate([{ $indexStats: {} }]). The stage must come first and takes an empty document. Rows include index name and key, originating host, accesses.ops and accesses.since; sharded output also identifies the shard. (high confidence)

Studio 3T's article distinguishes the two tools: Visual Explain (built on explain output) shows whether an index is in use for a particular query, whereas $indexStats shows how often an index comes into play. Sources: https://studio3t.com/whats-new/are-my-mongodb-indexes-being-used-studio3t_ama/

An OpenTelemetry receiver issue reported direct shard-member monitoring still issuing IndexStats despite disabled database metrics, using Splunk Collector 0.127.0. This is a version-specific monitoring caveat, not proof of current behavior. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-06)

Percona PMM documents that its unused-index advisor requires the indexStats metric collector. Missing advisor evidence can therefore reflect collection configuration rather than an absence of index usage. (low confidence)

$indexStats accesses counters are local to the node executing the query. Usage on a secondary is not recorded on the primary or other members; inspect every relevant replica-set member before declaring an index unused. (high confidence)

MongoDB issue SERVER-96438, updated October 12, 2026 and recorded as unresolved, describes mongos collecting results across shard primaries while omitting secondaries. Its request for all-node results is proposed behavior, not evidence that the feature exists. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-12)
accesses.ops counts user operations using an index; TTL deletions and chunk split or migration activity are excluded. It is not a count of indexed documents. (low confidence)

Methodological inference: $indexStats output includes name, key, host, shard and spec, and the accesses counters apply only to the node that ran the query. Running it through mongos returns results only from the primaries, leaving out secondaries (per an open MongoDB Jira improvement request), so summing mongos-returned rows alone should not be presented as all-member coverage; run $indexStats on each node and retain collection namespace, index spec, shard and host before rolling up. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexStats.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-96438

Methodological inference: $indexStats reports only per-index usage counters, whereas explain("executionStats") reports the index used and the number of documents scanned for a specific query. To assess whether a particular query is covered, use explain executionStats rather than the counters alone. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md

Historical counterexample: a MongoDB 3.2.11 incident report describes worse performance after dropping zero-counter indexes. The issue was closed as a duplicate of a checkpoint-related drop issue; it does not establish that current indexStats counters are defective. (low confidence)
